summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V15.4.1 as modified, moved from 4.0.3 V1.11.3 and merged from V1.11.2. V1.11.2 asked that high-value business logic flows (authentication, session management, access control) not share unsynchronized state. V1.11.3 asked that those same flows be thread-safe and resistant to TOCTOU race conditions. The current clause is about shared objects in multi-threaded code (caches, files, in-memory objects) and thread-safe types, locks, or semaphores.

The mapping notes predecessor text is dissimilar and git diverges from the ID slot. Mapping and predecessor wording are still the reliable origin. Ralph Andalis (csfreak92) opened #737 on 17 April 2020 because "unsynchronized state" was unclear to pentesters; Jim Manico first wanted the requirement deleted, then accepted a CWE-362 race-condition reading after Elar Lang pointed at that CWE.

On 6 May 2021 jim and ralph.andalis92 edited V1.11.2 in the architecture chapter. On 21–22 June 2022 Josh Grossman tried to clarify 1.11.2 based on #737 (commits 7f298c25 and 3c6ce8d2). 5.0 then merged 1.11.2 and 1.11.3 into a threading-and-shared-objects requirement, dropping "unsynchronized state" and the authentication/session/access-control examples. Elar Lang had warned in #737 that the rewrite was drifting toward the separate race-condition controls (then 1.11.3 / 11.1.6). Cookie-prefix stamps in the timeline are slot reuse.

Issue #737 shows a split over V1.11.2: Jim Manico argued the "unsynchronized state" requirement made no sense and should be deleted; Elar Lang argued against deleting a control whose CWE (362) was race conditions, and later noted that proposed rewordings were collapsing into the existing race-condition requirements. Josh Grossman later tried a clarification rather than deletion. 5.0's shared-objects wording is the outcome of that unresolved 4.x debate, not a documented consensus on the old phrase.

terminology.statement: "Unsynchronized state" in V1.11.2 was never defined in the standard; #737 treated it as race-condition / CWE-362 language and 5.0 replaced it with shared objects and synchronization mechanisms.

key_sources.role: debate over "unsynchronized state" that drove the 1.11.2 clarification
